summary: Charles Augustus Kincaid was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He was educated at Sherborne School around 1884 to 1889 and Balliol College, Oxford, from around 1889 to 1891.

Charles B. Jones works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD in History of Religions under Paul Groner at the University of Virginia (1996) and served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at Catholic University of America.

Linguist Charles Bally studied at the University of Geneva and Humboldt University of Berlin (dr.ph.), also studying under Ferdinand de Saussure. He taught at Collège Calvin (1900–1913) and the University of Geneva (1893–1939), where he succeeded Saussure.
Charles Barbier de Meynard studied under Julius Mohl and worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was attested in 1894 as a Membre de l'Institut at the Institut de France.
Charles Bowles was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Having succeeded John Shakespear, he served as Professor of Hindustani at Addiscombe Military Seminary from around 1845 to 1861.

Indologist Charles Bruce studied at Harrow, Yale, Westminster, and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the British Museum, King's College London, Royal College Curepipe, Royal College Port-Louis, and the UK Government.

Charles Burnett studied at the University of Cambridge before pursuing a career in history, archaeology, and philosophy. He held fellowships and research posts at St John's College, Sheffield, and the IAS, and became Professor at the Warburg Institute in 1999.
Indologist Charles Chapman studied at Hoxton Academy and with the traditional teacher Mahesha. He was a founder of The Asiatic Society.

Charles Cutler Torrey, who studied under Theodor Nöldeke, worked in religious studies, history, and linguistics. He founded the American Schools of Oriental Research in 1901 and taught at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900) and Yale University (1900–1932).

Charles D. Orzech completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago and specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He served as religious studies chair at UNC Greensboro (attested 1998–2006) and was a National Humanities Center Fellow.

Charles DiSimone, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD from the University of Munich by 2016. He later held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2021) and Ghent University (attested 2026).

Charles Duroiselle, a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Indology, co-founded the Burma Research Society. He held posts with the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940), the Archaeological Survey of India, and served as Professor at the University of Rangoon.

Charles Edmund Godakumbura earned degrees through a D.Litt. from the University of London. In Buddhist studies, Indology, and history, he taught at London and Ceylon, served as Archaeological Survey of India Commissioner (1956–1967), and presided over RAS Sri Lanka.

Charles Egbert Kennet studied at Bishop's College, Calcutta, working in religious studies and Indology. He served as teacher and Principal (1877) at Madras Theological College, and was a Fellow at the University of Madras (~1877–1884).

Charles Eliot studied at Cheltenham College and Balliol College, Oxford. Active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology, he held posts at the Foreign Office, served as Vice-Chancellor of Sheffield (~1905–1912), and led the University of Hong Kong (1912–1918).
Charles Elliott, active in Indology, studied at Fort William College (~1801–1804). He served with the East India Company (~1795–1830) and was Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1836–1856).

Charles Evelyn Arbuthnot William Oldham studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1888–1890). In Indology and history/archaeology, he was Assistant Editor for Indian Antiquary (~1925–1931) and Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (1935–1941).

Charles Gabriel Seligman studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School. Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he was Lecturer and then Chair of Ethnology at the London School of Economics and University of London (1913–1934).

Charles Georges Marcel Autran was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut Français d'Archéologie Orientale, and served as a professor at Aix-Marseille University.
Charles Godfrey Chenevix Trench was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his BA studies at Lincoln College, University of Oxford, around 1896 to 1900.
